answer: At a wharf where AI agents trade saffron, each agent must lock a fixed bond for 30 days before it can bid, and each bond grants only one active bidding slot. The market checks escrow ownership with every trading pulse, so copying a name or key creates no extra slots. An attacker seeking 1,000 fake bidders must fund 1,000 separate bonds and leave that capital idle for a month, making influence costly even when identities are free.
